summary.intent: Execute GSD phase 20 (vault-migration) with 4 plans implementing vault blob v2 binary format across TypeScript core, API server, Rust desktop, and web client. After execution, run a security review of all phase 20 code and fix any critical/high findings.
summary.outcome: All 4 plans executed successfully across 3 waves. Security review found 0 critical, 2 high issues; both high issues were fixed (input bounds validation on serializers, sensitive field redaction in Debug impls). All 165 TS tests and 10 Rust unit tests pass post-fix.

repo: Phase 20 work lives in a separate worktree/directory `cipher-box-phase-20`, not in the main `cipher-box` repo — gsd-tools init must be run from the correct working directory
The vault blob v2 format is implemented in three separate packages: @cipherbox/core (TS), the NestJS API server, and the Rust desktop FUSE app — all must be kept in sync
useAuth.ts implements a two-path login: PATH A for migrated users (IPFS v2 blob via IPNS) and PATH B for non-migrated users (lazy migration after normal login)
The API exposes POST /vault/migrate for server-side migration tracking; desktop Rust publishes v2 blobs to IPNS directly
Rust vault_blob.rs serialize_vault_blob_v2 originally returned bare bytes; after security fix it returns Result to surface bounds violations

code.finding: serialize_vault_blob_v2 was changed from returning Vec<u8> to Result<Vec<u8>, Error> to enforce key length bounds checks — all callers in commands/vault.rs and fuse/mod.rs required updating to propagate the error
InitVaultRequest and VaultResponse had #[derive(Debug)] which would expose sensitive key material in logs; replaced with custom Debug impls that redact those fields
TypeScript serializer for v2 blob needed explicit key length bounds validation mirroring the Rust implementation
Call site for serialize_vault_blob_v2 needed ? operator or explicit error propagation after function signature change to Result
Second call site for serialize_vault_blob_v2 in FUSE module also required error propagation update

workflow: GSD orchestrator must be initialized from the correct working directory — if gsd-tools init returns phase_found: false, check for separate phase worktrees
The security:review skill integrates naturally as a checkpoint step between wave execution and final verification; scope can be passed via ARGUMENTS
When Rust functions change return types to Result, test calls in the same file need .unwrap() — a quick grep for all call sites prevents missed updates
Spot-checking after each wave (SUMMARY.md exists + git commits present + no Self-Check: FAILED) is critical before proceeding to dependent waves

friction: API connection error (ConnectionRefused) on the first security:review invocation required a full retry
gsd-tools init defaulted to wrong directory (cipher-box instead of cipher-box-phase-20), requiring manual detection and re-run

Changing serialize_vault_blob_v2 to return Result required cascading updates across 3 files (commands/vault.rs, fuse/mod.rs, test calls in vault_blob.rs) — not all were immediately obvious from a single grep
open_items: 3 medium and 2 low security findings from the review were documented but not fixed — see .planning/security/REVIEW-2026-03-24-phase20.md

Human verification of the web client checkpoint (login with non-migrated account, re-login after migration, recovery.html testing) was requested but user approval was not captured in the transcript before the security review was triggered
Phase 20 verification (gsd-verifier) and roadmap update were not reached — the session ended mid-checkpoint after the security fix commit
